title: Wagner built an opera house where the orchestra plays hidden under the stage

cover.alt: The Bayreuth Festspielhaus, a plain brick and timber-framed opera house on a green hill, seen beyond a garden of purple, white and yellow flowers.

body: Richard Wagner adapted the design of the Festspielhaus in Bayreuth, Germany, from an unbuilt plan by Gottfried Semper, purely for his own stage works; it opened in August 1876 with the complete four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen, and his operas are still the only ones performed there. Its most unusual feature is the orchestra pit, recessed under the stage and covered by a hood, so the **orchestra is completely invisible** to the audience. The design also corrects the balance of volume between singers and orchestra, and the first violins’ sound reaches the audience by bouncing off the back of the stage. Wagner called the gap the pit and a double proscenium create between audience and stage a ‘mystic gulf’.

slides.prompt: Playing in the pit of Wagner’s opera house in Bayreuth, Germany, comes with an unusual problem. What is it?
slides.answer: Most can’t see or hear the singers
slides.detail: The reverberation also makes it hard to keep orchestra and singers together, so conductors must train themselves to ignore cues from the singers.

slides.question: Who provided most of the money to build the Festspielhaus, Wagner’s Bayreuth opera house?
slides.explanation: Ludwig II of Bavaria provided the primary funding for the building.
